claims.statement: Each src/ format module is a thin adapter between the CommonRomfile trait system and one backend: archive (sevenz-rust2 + zip), rvz/wbfs (nod), xso (xso-rs), nsz (nsz-rs), gdi (gdi-rs), xdelta (xdelta-rs), xps (xps-rs) run in-process, while chdman (CHD) and ctrtool (CIA) shell out to executables on PATH.

Built-in backends return the literal string "built-in" from get_version() because a linked library has no runtime version to query; chdman and ctrtool return a version parsed from their output, and gdi, iso, wbfs and crc32 export no get_version() at all.

nsz::get_version() reports "built-in, prod.keys not found" when ~/.switch/prod.keys is absent, since only compressing NSPs holding NCAs needs keys, so the gap is surfaced before rather than during a compression.

In the conversion and export paths every format is treated as available except CHD, which is probed through util::tool_available(chdman::get_version); ctrtool availability is checked separately only where CIA files are imported.

chdman feature availability is gated on its parsed version, not just its presence: MIN_SPLITBIN_VERSION 0.265 for multi-track CHDs and MIN_DREAMCAST_VERSION 0.264 for Dreamcast CHD creation, with callers skipping the game and warning rather than running a command the installed tool cannot perform.

Format modules follow a fixed pattern: As* validates and wraps an existing file (some by extension, as_xso/as_chd/as_riff/as_rdsk by magic via get_mimetype), To* produces a file and returns a wrapper re-validated through the matching As*, and compressed formats implement HashAndSize/Check by decoding into a temp directory and delegating.

progress::run_blocking is the single adapter that runs a synchronous, CPU-bound format crate on the tokio blocking pool behind a bytes progress bar whose length is the input bytes the crate reports consuming; a panic in the blocking task surfaces as "Conversion task failed", distinct from the crate's own error.

archive.rs edits containers by copying entries already encoded: ZIP rewrites with raw_copy_file/raw_copy_file_rename, and 7z copies whole surviving blocks with push_raw_block so pack sizes stay bit-identical, re-encoding only a solid block that loses some of its entries.

A rewrite that leaves no entries deletes the archive: replace removes the scratch file and the original when zero entries are kept, and ArchiveRomfile::delete_file then removes the archive file once it parses empty.

Appending to an existing archive preserves the original encoded blocks: create uses ZipWriter::new_append for ZIP and rewrite_sevenzip with an add closure for 7z, and the solid parameter is unused because one entry arrives per call (batching a game into one solid block is a documented TODO).
Rewriting a 7z preserves its codec: is_zstd inspects the block coders and re-applies Zstandard at the default level 19, so a zstd archive does not drift back to LZMA2.

Zstandard archives are readable and writable only in archive.rs: get_archive_compression maps SEVENZIP_/ZIP_COMPRESSION_ALGORITHM plus separate 1-22 zstd level keys (default 19, RomVault's level) and 1-9 levels for the other codecs onto ArchiveCompression, and neither the zip nor sevenz-rust2 crate is used anywhere else in src/.

7z extraction decodes the whole block containing the wanted entry and drains entries it is not after into io::sink, because solid-block entries share a single stream; copy_files_between_archives calls ZipWriter::finish explicitly so a central-directory write failure cannot be swallowed by a dropped writer.
ArchiveRomfile carries each entry's size and CRC from the archive listing, so a CRC check of a file inside a container is answered without extracting it.

wbfs.rs is a thin caller of rvz.rs::write_disc with FormatOptions::new(Format::Wbfs), so WBFS shares nod's disc opening, writer-thread sizing and header finalization and adds no compression, block size or settings keys of its own.

rvz::write_disc finalizes RVZ/WBFS by rewinding the output and rewriting the header after all blocks are written, sizes progress from writer.progress_bound() (progress through the source, not bytes written), and allocates processor threads from the writer's DiscWriterWeight (0, min(cores,4), or all cores).

rvz::open pins PartitionEncryption::Original so a decoded disc reproduces the source exactly, letting RvzRomfile hash a disc by streaming the DiscReader through common::hash_reader instead of writing several gigabytes of decoded ISO to the temp directory; Check takes the extract-to-ISO route only when a DAT declares a header.

RVZ_SCRUB is accepted but ignored with the warning "RVZ_SCRUB is unsupported by nod, writing unscrubbed" because write_disc hardcodes ScrubLevel::None; convert_roms never reads the key and passes false, while export_roms still uses it to decide whether an existing RVZ is copied verbatim or re-encoded through a temp ISO.

RVZ compression mapping clamps rather than rejects levels: RVZ_COMPRESSION_LEVEL spans 1-22 which only Zstandard accepts, so bzip2/lzma/lzma2 are clamped to 1-9 to keep existing configurations working, and RVZ_BLOCK_SIZE is stored in KiB and multiplied by 1024 for nod.

ChdType (Cd/Dvd/Hd/Ld), parsed from chdman info metadata fourcc, drives everything in chdman.rs: the create/extract subcommand, the destination format (CD to CUE/BIN, DVD to ISO, HD to RDSK, LD to RIFF), and the rule that a CD-type CHD reports no size or hash of its own, forcing per-BIN verification.

CHD parents are resolved by content rather than name: as_chd reads Parent SHA1 and scans sibling CHDs until one reports a matching SHA1, while as_chd_with_parent takes a caller-supplied parent (from the database parent_id via transcode::romfile_as_chd) and fails on a mismatch.

The CIA path is a ctrtool listing plus certificate surgery in oxyromon: parse_cia scrapes TitleVersion/TitleMetaSize/ContentId+Size and appends a synthetic tmd.{version} entry sized as TMD plus 0x300 TMD cert plus 0x400 CA cert, and extract_files_from_cia appends those certificates to the extracted tmd file itself.

Both ctrtool entry points deliberately bypass util::run_tool and tolerate the specific stdout error "NcchHeader is corrupted (Bad struct magic)", because that is the expected result of -p on a non-homebrew title; removing the allowance breaks retail CIA imports.

nsz_rs is given load_keys as a lazy loader rather than a key set, so decompression (unverified) never loads keys and compression loads ~/.switch/prod.keys only when NCAs require them; keys are CRC-verified so a tampered file is rejected rather than producing garbage output.

nsz.rs records the exact equivalence to the subprocess calls it replaced: to_nsp equals `nsz -D -F` (fix_padding true, verify false, strict false) and to_nsz equals `nsz -C -K -L -P` (solid stream, ldm true, level 18, fix_padding false), with -K inherent to the crate and -P only needed by the Python tool.

iso.rs is in-repo Rust (a port of bchunk), not a crate: it parses the CUE the way bchunk does and copies only 2048 bytes of user data per 2352-byte sector for the first track only, refusing non-MODE1/2352 and MODE2/2352 tracks and a BIN too short for the described range; it also hosts the vendored iso9660 reader used by import-irds.

xdelta.rs and xps.rs implement common::Patch, which is not wired into any production path (both wrappers and As* traits are allow(dead_code) and only their own tests call them); xps surfaces xps_rs::apply's optional warning as "Patched, but ...".

crc32.rs adapts crc32fast to both the digest traits and std::io::Write, which is what allows common::hash_reader to pipe any decoder's output through progress_bar.wrap_write and thus hash a stream (such as a decoding disc image) as CRC32.

The dependency table shown by info, the GraphQL dependencies query and the MCP status payload is one hard-coded list keyed by backend name (sevenz-rust2, chdman, ctrtool, xps-rs, xso-rs, nsz-rs, xdelta-rs, nod), with gdi and iso absent, and a failing get_version rendered as "not found" / a null version.
